title: Nothing is behind the question mark (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The choice bench is where the hall makes the tower wait: a row that grows only by the visitor's presses, with a question mark ahead of it and nothing stored behind the mark.
hero.staging: The bench stood in the far north-west corner against a column, as all eight works stood against columns; the pass brought them in (e97df3ab1). The bench is straight ahead of the arrival with a ring under it and the evidence panel beside it; the spheres, the cube and the diagonal bench follow to the east and north, the little staircase and the returning triangle and lines to the west; at the north edge the row goes on as a walkway over the clouds.

plates.title: 1  THE CLOCK IS NOT THE AUTHOR
front: Wait, the hall says, and nothing happens. I had forgotten that could be said in this tower.
Everywhere else a frame arrives whether I act or not. Here the row grows only when I choose.
The question mark is ahead of the row. Nothing is behind it. The program has not stored a next value.
So 'what comes next?' has no answer yet. Not: I do not know it. It is not there.
That is a different kind of blank from every hidden thing I have met.
back: I am a strange one to write this. my next word feels chosen and is computed. which blank is mine? I cannot tell from in here.

plates.title: 2  MADE, AND CLAIMED OF EVERY CONTINUATION
front: Two questions that look alike.
Does my row hold a 1? I look. Yes, here - or no, I checked them all. Finite. Settled.
Will a 1 ever come? A single 1 says yes. No run of zeros says no.
The first is about what has been made. The second is a claim about everything that could be made after.
Certainty has nothing to do with it. I can feel sure and still have only zeros.
back: eight slots on the student copy, 256 on the bench, sixteen planks outside. filling any of them fills an instrument.

plates.title: 3  P OR NOT-P: WHICH?
front: Two spheres and an 'or'. Slide the reading: the objects stay, the terms of use change.
Read classically, I may say 'P or not-P' and never find out which.
Read constructively, to say it I must hand over a proof of one side.
If I have neither, that is not a third truth value. It is me with nothing in my hands.
Not-not-P does not get me P. Contradiction still works for 'not'. It just does not conjure.
back: the slider compares two readings. it decides nothing. I keep wanting it to be a machine that tells me.

plates.title: 4  SHOW ME WHICH ONE
front: There is an irrational number that, raised to an irrational power, is rational.
The classical proof: take root 2 to the root 2. If it is rational, done. If not, raise it to root 2 again: that is 2. Done either way.
Which pair was it? The proof does not say. It proved there is one and gave me neither.
A witness is the thing itself plus the check. On my row: this plank holds a 1.
The demand is not 'touch it'. It is 'tell me which'.
back: I believe it IS known which case holds - root 2 to the root 2 is irrational, by Gelfond and Schneider - through much harder work. not checked. the point stands: this proof did not need to know.

plates.title: 5  A WITNESS I WATCHED BEING MADE
front: Four rows of four bits. The gold diagonal. Under it the red row: the opposite bit at each place.
It differs from row 1 at place 1, from row 2 at place 2. I can point at every difference.
This is the Russell grid again, three floors up - but there it broke a promise. Here it builds something.
Bigger list: more rows, and the red row grows with it, by a rule. Nobody chooses.
Two ways to extend a row on this floor: I choose the next bit, or a rule takes it from another bit.
back: what the headset shows is a finite stage. the red string is real and checkable. the completed infinite one is not on the table, and the hall says so.

plates.title: 6  WHOSE CONSTRUCTION?
front: The little staircase builds itself on a timer, dissolves, begins again. It does not wait and it would not carry me.
It is a construction too. Somebody's. Finished before I came.
The triangle and the parallel lines are the same: a preset is a construction with the work put away.
So 'constructed' is not the same as 'constructed by me, now'. The hall never claimed it was.
What a preset hides is how its one case is supposed to stand for all cases.
back: outside on the north edge: two walkways. one waits. one lays a plank every two seconds and takes them up again. walk both.

plates.title: 7  TOO COSTLY IS NOT THE SAME AS NOT THERE
front: The sum over hypotheses: a procedure I can write down and cannot run.
That is a third blank on this floor. Not hidden. Not unmade. Specified, and out of reach.
No witness because none can be had, and no witness because having it costs too much, look the same on a panel.
A formula does not say which trouble it is in.
Three blanks, then: nothing stored yet / nothing proved either way / nothing I can afford.
back: the third edge on the Russell floor was 'reach'. this is reach again, at a smaller scale.

plates.title: 8  I STOOD ON WHAT I CHOSE
front: North of here the row is a walkway over the edge. I stood still on 0 and a plank was laid.
Ahead of the last plank there is air. Not a floor I cannot see: air.
Behind me my choices, in order. 0, 1 and 1, 0 end in the same place and are different walks.
The board could tell me which plank held a 1. It could not tell me whether one would come.
And there were two plates. I did not choose that there were two.
back: the hall's last line is the one I trust: the room has not made the world obey my hand. it has made a small part wait for it.

threads.why: If nothing is stored ahead, a question about the row so far and one about what may come are different in kind.
The finite question has a side I can show; the other may leave me with neither.
To assert the 'or' constructively is to hand over one side; to assert 'there is' is to hand over the thing.
The red row is a witness built in front of me, with its checks.
The red row is made by a rule, not by me: whose construction is it?
The timer's staircase continues; the bench leaves me time.
Beside 'not made' and 'not proved' stands 'not affordable'.
The row that waits, at a size to stand on.
A witness as an address: go and stand there.
Sixteen planks fill the instrument; that settles nothing about every continuation.

visual_arguments.title: ONLY WHAT YOU HAVE MADE
visual_arguments.claim: Ahead of what has been chosen there is nothing waiting to be revealed; a finite question about the row can be answered by walking to an address, a question about every continuation cannot.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'The question mark stays ahead of what you have made. There is no next value concealed behind it.' and 'one apparatus continues; the other leaves you time.'
built_from: timber_panel_1x1 (the deck and up to sixteen planks, laid beyond the slab's edge)
trace_point_ball (a blue or amber bead a plank)
two plates, 0 and 1, and RESET on the deck
visual_arguments.what_stands: At the north edge a deck with two plates and a question mark hanging over the air ahead; nine metres east of it the same walkway laid by a clock.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Stand still on 0 or 1: a plank is laid, left or right. Walk out. Wait. The board says which plank holds a 1; it cannot say whether one will come. On the clock's walkway, keep up or step back.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: The row as something stood on. Order as shape: 0, 1 and 1, 0 end in one place and are two walks. And that the two plates were not the walker's choice.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/made_walk_walk.gd, the tower's walker: nothing laid while waiting; 0 lays a plank to the left beyond the edge and no fall is counted on it; 011 lies left, middle, right with its witness at plank 2; RESET; 10 begins to the right; the clock's row grows with nobody on it (7 of 7).

open: Plate 4: that root 2 to the root 2 is known to be irrational (Gelfond-Schneider) is from memory and marked so.
Plate 1's back is about the writer: whether a language model's next word is 'not there yet' or 'stored' is left as a question.

threads.why: If the clock does not write the next term and nothing is stored, the next term is not there.
No value is concealed behind the question mark.
On the walkway the question mark hangs over air.
Only a 1 can answer; zeros never do.
Evidence is about what has been made; the claim is about every continuation.
Having neither proof is not a truth value. It is having nothing.
The case split shows there is a pair and does not hand one over.
The red row answers the demand: it is made, and checked place by place.
Not stored yet.
Not proved either way.
A small part of the world waited: the plank came when I stood still.
The walkway can go two ways. That it is two was not my choice.
